findings.claim: Signed favorable-minus-comparison endpoint contrasts at the observed selection nodes are strongest and most reproducible for the short-range pair kernels: pair_kernel_1.5 (integrated z 0.562, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 1.0), pair_kernel_2.5 (0.631, q 2.2e-5, 1.0) and pair_kernel_3.5 (0.540, q 9.8e-5, 1.0), with pair_kernel_5.0 weaker (0.319, q 3.7e-3) and pair_kernel_7.0 reversed (-0.485, q 1.5e-4, positive batch fraction 0.0). The same ordering appears in the raw and adjusted branch correlations (e.g. pair_kernel_1.5 raw r 0.085, adjusted r 0.101; pair_kernel_2.5 raw 0.088, adjusted 0.084). This is selection enrichment of a radial pair-distance shell density, not an absolute geometric descriptor and not a physical interaction energy.

Shape anisotropy carries signed selection contrast: shape_yy is the most negative endpoint effect (integrated z -0.513, q 1.5e-5, positive batch fraction 0.0) and remains negative after branch adjustment (raw r -0.103, adjusted r -0.100, q 3e-4), while shape_xx (-0.495, q 8.1e-4) and shape_yz (-0.212, q 0.035) are weaker and shape_xz is positive (+0.185, q 0.22, not significant). The corresponding local_cyy regional enrichment is negative at nearly every landmark (e.g. landmark_00 -0.575, landmark_07 -0.646, landmark_16 -0.672, landmark_19 -0.622, all q<0.002). These are coordinate covariance descriptors, not inferred chemical mechanisms.

Landmark soft-minimum distances show mixed but reproducible signs: negative (closer) for landmark_00 (-0.481, q 8.1e-4), landmark_04 (-0.351, q 0.014), landmark_06 (-0.294, q 6.8e-4), landmark_15 (-0.357, q 2.6e-3) and landmark_18 (-0.311, q 3.8e-3), and positive (farther) for landmark_02 (+0.253, q 4.6e-3), landmark_03 (+0.360, q 0.013), landmark_05 (+0.396, q 2.9e-3), landmark_12 (+0.335, q 0.012) and landmark_17 (+0.312, q 0.049). The soft_mass enrichment is positive at landmark_00 (+0.639, q 1.9e-4), landmark_07 (+0.481, q 7.4e-3), landmark_10 (+0.395, q 3.7e-4) and landmark_17 (+0.312, q 0.054) and negative at landmark_11 (-0.322, q 0.023) and landmark_12 (-0.257, q 0.029). Lower soft-min distance does not by itself establish a quality benefit.

Descendant survival credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity. Its signs partly agree with the selection contrasts (landmark_00_soft_mass +0.365, q 0.12; landmark_07_soft_mass +0.220, q 0.36; landmark_10_soft_mass +0.234, q 0.30; landmark_18_local_czz +0.217, q 0.30) but several survival effects are negative where selection was positive or vice versa (landmark_05_local_czz -0.419, q 0.12; landmark_09_local_czz -0.390, q 0.12; landmark_14_local_czz -0.308, q 0.12; landmark_16_local_cyy -0.317, q 0.22). Because decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable, last-record survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Parent-child increment contrasts are noisier than the population contrasts and only a few survive multiplicity adjustment: shape_xx (-3.70, q 0.095), shape_yy (-3.85, q 0.16), shape_xz (+3.00, q 0.21), pair_kernel_2.5 (+3.96, q 0.21), pair_kernel_7.0 (-3.14, q 0.21), landmark_00_softmin (-4.91, q 0.046) and landmark_00_occupancy3 (+4.28, q 0.081). The increment evidence therefore supports within-path change for landmark_00 and shape_xx more than for the pair kernels, and does not license treating the increment as a causal selection effect.

Turnover accounting separates population rate, parent-edge rate and their residual. For landmark_00_local_cxx the population rate is near zero (-0.058) while the edge rate is strongly negative (-4.34, q 0.055) and the residual is strongly positive (+4.29, q 0.038); the same pattern appears for landmark_00_local_cyy (population +0.258, edge -4.79, residual +5.05, q 0.033), landmark_04_local_cxx (population +1.08, edge -4.60, residual +5.67, q 0.012), landmark_07_local_cxx (population +0.38, edge -4.69, residual +5.08, q 0.012), landmark_08_local_cxx (population +0.43, edge -5.12, residual +5.54, q 0.012), landmark_16_local_cyy (population +0.46, edge -5.90, residual +6.37, q 0.012), landmark_17_local_cxx (population +0.43, edge -4.82, residual +5.24, q 0.012) and landmark_19_local_cxx (population +0.48, edge -4.82, residual +5.30, q 0.012). The residual is an accounting diagnostic that includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not a causal selection effect or an atom velocity.

The supplied continuous contrast functions are observed-node linear interpolations over the complete observed window [0.0,0.49] with extrapolation disallowed, and they are not absolute reward targets. Across the landmark_00 and landmark_01 families the first and last rate z-scores frequently have opposite signs (e.g. landmark_00_local_dx first -17.5, last +8.1; landmark_00_local_dy first -72.4, last +5.5; landmark_01_local_dz first -58.5, last +8.8; landmark_01_local_cyy first -40.6, last +19.7), and the reported sign-change counts are large (4 to 10) with strong sign conflicts (1 to 18). A constant rule is therefore not supported by these curves; a time-conditioned rule would need validated fits, and the supplied polynomial fits were not accepted.

The curve-fidelity audit selected only 24 of the candidate curves under the rule relative_rmse_le 0.35, strong_sign_conflict_nodes_eq 0, quiet_node_large_fit_fraction_le 0.1, absolute_integrated_z_ge 0.1, batch_direction_fraction_ge 0.857 and q_lt 0.05. The landmark_00 and landmark_01 local families fail that rule: their relative node RMSE values are 0.29 to 0.99 and their strong sign-conflict counts are 1 to 18, and the audit records legendre_runtime_allowed false for every listed curve. The surviving curves are the short-range pair kernels and a subset of shape and landmark soft-min/occupancy fields.

Joint-motion diagnostics are the most reproducible negative effects in the branch-adjusted tables: joint_innovation_RMS_A (raw covariance -5.15e-5, q 0.038, same-sign batch fraction 0.857; adjusted covariance -3.60e-5, q 0.020, 0.929; raw correlation -0.142, q 9.3e-5, 1.0; adjusted correlation -0.150, q 2.8e-4, 0.929) and joint_internal_RMS_A (raw covariance -5.00e-5, q 0.044; adjusted covariance -3.42e-5, q 0.030; raw correlation -0.130, q 1.5e-4; adjusted correlation -0.137, q 1.3e-5). joint_translation_RMS_A is weaker (adjusted covariance -8.99e-6, q 0.072; adjusted correlation -0.076, q 0.052). These are adjusted branch covariance and correlation diagnostics, not rigid-motion residuals of the region moments themselves.

Within-selector joint diagnostics show that innovation is coherent with the teacher contrast rather than with observed child score gain: teacher_innovation_contrast_alignment is +0.226 (q 2.2e-9, positive batch fraction 1.0) and innovation_native_alignment is +0.092 (q 2.2e-9, 1.0), whereas observed_child_score_gain is -0.036 (q 1.8e-7, positive batch fraction 0.0). The teacher contrast is dominated by its internal fraction (0.787) with smaller translation (0.132) and rotation (0.081) fractions. These are descriptive within-selector associations with batch as the independent unit, not causal affinity effects.

The information audit reports that the compressed geometric choice exceeds the fixed-frame Hungarian RMS by 0.081 A (CI 0.070 to 0.092) and that the compressed chosen teacher score correlation is 0.102 (CI 0.065 to 0.140) versus 0.064 for the full set, with top-4 teacher overlap 0.470. The audit explicitly limits these to nonnegative excess distance by construction, not a causal affinity effect, and notes that teacher score correlations are observational and not a fitted or independently validated affinity predictor. The lineage support records 14 complete survival batches, BH correction jointly over 400 survival field/measure tests, 349 nodes with fewer than 3 ancestors and 531 with fewer than 6, and terminal metadata at index 99 with one future resampling node per batch.

Scope limits that constrain every finding above: the learning window and curve support are [0.0,0.5] and [0.0,0.49] with 50 observed score times; decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable; recorded affinities were removed with an equal score prior; the coordinate representation is the native model endpoint world frame; and the observable definitions state that these are endpoint forecast descriptors, not atom velocities, neural attention, physical energies or causal affinity gradients. The formula registry states that the executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term, so the pair-kernel and moment effects are diagnostic evidence only.

hypotheses.claim: Testable coordinate hypothesis: the short-range pair-distance shell density (pair_kernel_1.5 to 3.5) is the most reproducible signed selection contrast, with the long-range shell (pair_kernel_7.0) reversed. Observable: favorable-minus-comparison pair_kernel_a contrast at the observed selection nodes. Intended response: increasing short-range shell density while decreasing the 7.0 A shell density. Target origin: the observed selection-node coordinate cloud in the native endpoint world frame. Scale: pair distances 1.5 to 3.5 A versus 7.0 A. Discriminating failure condition: if the short-range and long-range signs do not separate in an independent batch set, or if the effect disappears after branch adjustment, the hypothesis is not supported. This remains descriptive unless a permitted reward recipe can express it; the executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel term.

Testable coordinate hypothesis: reduced shape_yy (and to a lesser degree shape_xx) anisotropy is a reproducible signed selection contrast, concentrated in the local_cyy regional field at nearly all landmarks. Observable: favorable-minus-comparison shape_yy and local_cyy contrasts. Intended response: decreasing shape_yy while leaving shape_xz and shape_xy free, since shape_xz is positive and not significant and shape_xy is near zero. Target origin: the endpoint shape covariance in the common receptor frame. Scale: A^2 covariance entries. Discriminating failure condition: a batch in which shape_yy is positive or in which the adjusted correlation loses its sign would weaken the direction. This is a coordinate covariance descriptor, not an inferred chemical mechanism.

Testable temporal hypothesis: the landmark_00 and landmark_01 local contrast curves change sign within the observed window, so a time-conditioned rule would differ from a constant rule. Observable: the observed-node linear contrast values at the 50 shared score times. Intended response: a rule whose direction follows the observed sign of the curve rather than a fixed sign. Target origin: the validated observed-node interpolation only, with no extrapolation beyond [0.0,0.49]. Scale: the full observed window. Discriminating failure condition: if the first and last rate z-scores agree in sign across independent batches, or if the curve-fidelity audit accepts a constant fit, the time-conditioned rule is not supported. The supplied polynomial fits were not accepted and Legendre runtime use is disallowed.

Testable accounting hypothesis: for the local_cxx and local_cyy fields the population rate is near zero while the parent-edge rate is strongly negative and the turnover residual is strongly positive, which is consistent with changing cohort composition or reclassification rather than within-path change. Observable: population_rate, edge_rate and turnover_residual_rate per feature. Intended response: none directly; this is an accounting diagnostic. Target origin: the parent-debiased moment strata and compact credit table. Scale: whole window. Discriminating failure condition: if the residual is not reproducible across independent batches, or if the edge rate and population rate agree in sign, the composition explanation is not supported. The residual is not a causal selection effect or an atom velocity.

Testable joint-geometry hypothesis: coherent joint coordinate patterns (joint_innovation_RMS_A and joint_internal_RMS_A) carry reproducible negative selection contrast beyond common motion, while joint_translation_RMS_A is weaker, and the innovation is aligned with the teacher contrast rather than with observed child score gain. Observable: adjusted branch covariance and correlation of the joint RMS fields, and the within-selector innovation alignment metrics. Intended response: reducing joint innovation and internal RMS while retaining freedom in the surrounding coordinates. Target origin: the adjusted branch covariance diagnostics. Scale: Angstrom RMS. Discriminating failure condition: if the adjusted correlation loses its sign in an independent batch set, or if the innovation alignment with observed child score gain becomes positive, the hypothesis is not supported. These are adjusted branch diagnostics, not rigid-motion residuals of the region moments.

Testable survival hypothesis: descendant survival credit agrees with the selection contrast for landmark_00_soft_mass, landmark_07_soft_mass, landmark_10_soft_mass and landmark_18_local_czz but disagrees for landmark_05_local_czz, landmark_09_local_czz, landmark_14_local_czz and landmark_16_local_cyy. Observable: survival_enrichment_z per feature. Intended response: none directly; this is a comparison of selection enrichment with descendant survival credit. Target origin: the recorded joint-head credit table. Scale: whole window. Discriminating failure condition: if decoded terminal learning labels become available and the survival signs do not match the terminal affinity signs, the survival credit cannot be used as a final affinity proxy. Without decoded terminal labels this comparison is unavailable and the survival credit must not be presented as final affinity benefit.

limitations: Decoded terminal learning labels are unavailable; descendant credit is recorded joint-head credit, not decoded terminal affinity.
Turnover residual includes score reclassification and extant-parent weighting, not only resampling, and is an accounting diagnostic rather than a causal selection effect.
Adjusted branch covariance is supplied evidence; the region moments themselves are not rigid-motion residuals.
Curve fitting does not establish causal benefit or a gradient; no time bins or outside-window analysis is permitted.
Static teachers are last-learning-node forecasts, not actual final structures.
All weak and null scalar effects are retained; current study outcomes are withheld from design roles.
The executing pointcloud scalar has no pair-kernel, moment, joint-motif or geometry-block term, so those effects are diagnostic evidence only.
Temperatures are immutable task parameters and no temperature edit is proposed or implied.
